paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes PatchCue, a trained vision-language reasoning method using patch-level visual cues, cold-start SFT, GRPO, and a process-supervised cue reward.
dominant_domain: Vision-language reasoning, visual cue grounding, patch-level intermediate reasoning, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning.
must_cover: PatchCue replaces pixel-level visual cues with patch-bbox cues aligned to VLM patch tokenization.
The data pipeline filters challenging samples, extracts visual cues with GPT-4o, verifies grounding with strong VLMs, and reconstructs cue-guided reasoning.
Training uses 12K patch-cue samples plus 12K general QA samples for SFT, then 15K curated samples for GRPO.
The reward combines answer accuracy, output format, and a patch-level F1 cue reward.
Main results show consistent gains on Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MiMo-VL-7B.
Ablations compare cue format, data ratio, cue reward, and prior cue-based methods.
key_numbers: Qwen2.5-VL-7B average score improves from 70.1 to 72.1 with PatchCue.
MiMo-VL-7B average score improves from 73.9 to 75.4 with PatchCue.
Patch-bbox cue format reaches 71.6 average, higher than pixel-bbox 70.4, pixel-point 70.4, patch-point 70.4, and label-only 70.1.
Mixed SFT with Gen:Cue ratio 1:1 reaches AI2D 84.6, ChartQA 87.9, MMStar 65.6, and MMVP 78.7.
Cue-only SFT drops to AI2D 80.8, MMStar 60.3, and MMVP 68.0.
Adding cue reward in RL reaches AI2D 84.7, ChartQA 88.1, MMStar 66.2, and MMVP 79.3.
Under same backbone and about 12K SFT samples, PatchCue reaches AI2D 84.7, ChartQA 88.1, MMStar 66.2, and MMVP 79.3.
real_comparisons: Compared with text-only CoT, PatchCue gives the model explicit visual references during intermediate reasoning.
Compared with pixel-bbox cues, patch-bbox cues are coarser but better aligned with VLM input tokens.
Compared with point cues, patch-bbox cues preserve region extent and reduce precise localization burden.
Compared with VisualCoT, CogCom, and MINI-CoT under a matched SFT protocol, PatchCue gives the strongest reported scores.

central_claims.claim: Patch-level visual cues are a better intermediate representation than pixel boxes or points for VLM reasoning.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The controlled cue-format table shows patch-bbox has the highest average under the same data scale and training recipe.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove patch cues are optimal for every VLM architecture or every image resolution.

central_claims.claim: PatchCue's gains come from cue-guided training rather than only generic SFT.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: Data-ratio and reward ablations show cue data and cue reward improve selected benchmarks beyond generic-only training.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not fully isolate the effect of GPT-4o-generated reasoning text from the visual cue labels.

central_claims.claim: The framework generalizes across several VLM backbones.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The main table reports gains on Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MiMo-VL-7B.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not establish transfer to closed-source models or non-patch-tokenized architectures.

claim_boundaries: The cue data depends on GPT-4o and several strong VLMs for extraction and validation.
The largest gains are moderate on many general VQA metrics.
Cue-only SFT harms some benchmarks, so the method needs a general-data mixture.
The work reports trained behavior, not a training-free inference plugin.
negative_or_limiting_results: Cue-only SFT underperforms mixed SFT on AI2D, MMStar, and MMVP.
RL without the cue reward is weaker than RL with the cue reward.
PatchCue may still fail when the cue is localized correctly but reasoning is flawed.
Figure 10 was rejected by the visual quality gate because the crop is too small for reliable note insertion.
mechanism_result_map: Patch-bbox representation maps to stronger cue-format results by reducing coordinate precision burden.
Mixed SFT maps to better robustness because general QA data preserves instruction-following ability.
Patch-level F1 reward maps to better RL results because intermediate cue alignment is directly rewarded.
Validation by multiple VLMs maps to cleaner cue labels and fewer noisy training examples.
comparative_positioning: PatchCue sits in the Train line because it makes visual cue generation a learned model behavior.
It is closer to MINT-CoT than to VisRef: both train intermediate visual references rather than only editing inference.
Compared with Qwen-LA, PatchCue focuses on where to look during reasoning, not on reflection-time visual token reinsertion.
Compared with DeepEyes, PatchCue supervises cue structure more explicitly and relies less on emergent tool use.
reuse_takeaways: For 3D reasoning agents, patch-level cues suggest using voxel, view tile, or rendered-region IDs instead of raw pixel boxes.
Intermediate visual references should be evaluated with process rewards, not only final answer accuracy.
Cue data should be mixed with general data to avoid narrowing the model's response distribution.
Report cue-format ablations whenever claiming visual grounding gains.
followup_questions: Would patch-bbox cues still dominate if the base model uses a different visual tokenizer?
How much does GPT-4o cue extraction quality determine the final performance?
Can cue reward be made self-supervised without external VLM validators?
Would 3D patch or view-tile cues improve embodied spatial reasoning tasks?

section_plan.focus: Explain why text-only CoT underuses visual evidence and why pixel-level cues impose unnecessary localization difficulty.
Describe the cue data pipeline, the 12K cue and 12K general SFT mix, and the 15K GRPO set.
Cover patch-bbox conversion, structured output tags, cue reward, Hungarian matching, and final reward.
Use main results and ablations to show where PatchCue helps and where the gains are limited.
Interpret PatchCue as a tokenization-aligned compromise between precise localization and usable reasoning supervision.
Record dependency on generated cue labels, moderate gains, cue-only degradation, and unresolved causal grounding concerns.
